title: For the ones who chose
hook: a blessing for the righteous, the pious and sincere converts

segments.voice: Yesterday, the blessing against harm, and Beruriah's let sins cease. Your line was end the harm. Today, the blessing that comes right after it, for the good.

A man named Obadiah, who has become a Jew, writes a letter to Moses Maimonides, in Egypt. His question is about the Amidah. Every day it begins: our God and God of our fathers, God of Abraham. But Obadiah's fathers weren't Abraham's children. Should he change the words, and say God of your fathers? Or say nothing at that line at all? Is he saying something untrue three times a day? Maimonides' answer is still read today.
screen: `A LETTER TO MAIMONIDES.` → `GOD OF OUR FATHERS?` → `SOMETHING UNTRUE, THREE TIMES A DAY?`

segments.voice: Maimonides writes back: say it exactly as written. Abraham is your father too. He's the father of everyone who comes under the wings of the Divine Presence. By custom, converts are named son or daughter of Abraham and Sarah. And in the thirteenth blessing of the Amidah, the community names them in its prayer: on the righteous, on the pious, on the elders of Your people, on the remnant of their scholars, on the righteous converts, and on us, may Your compassion be stirred. Give good reward to all who truly trust in Your name, and place our portion with them. Blessed are You, support and trust of the righteous. Look at that list. The converts, gerei hatzedek, stand right next to the righteous and the scholars. And the last item: and on us. The ordinary person praying adds themselves at the end of the list, hoping to belong in that company. The Torah tells Israel to love the stranger, the ger, a word the rabbis also use for a convert. In the old Jewish translation: "Love ye therefore the stranger; for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt." And Ruth, whom tradition remembers as a convert, says to Naomi: "thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God." Her great-grandson is King David. In this blessing, the people who chose stand in the community's daily prayer.
screen: `MAIMONIDES: ABRAHAM IS YOUR FATHER.` · `THE RIGHTEOUS, THE PIOUS, THE CONVERTS.` · `AND ON US.` · `RUTH: THY PEOPLE SHALL BE MY PEOPLE.` · then, large: `FOR THE ONES WHO CHOSE.`

segments.voice: Remember someone who chose to join a people, a family or a community they weren't born into: a convert you know, an in-law who learned all the family recipes, a neighbor who became a citizen. Think of what it cost them, the learning, the questions, the moments of feeling outside, and hold them with respect for a few breaths. If you pray, you can include them in this blessing.
Gerei hatzedek. Righteous converts, named in the Amidah's thirteenth blessing beside the righteous, the pious and the scholars, and then, at the end, us.
Your line: right beside the righteous. Abraham is their father too. Day five hundred ninety, done.

howItsDone: Al hatzaddikim is the thirteenth blessing of the weekday Amidah, praying for the righteous, the pious, the elders, the scholars and righteous converts; converts to Judaism say the Amidah with the same words, God of our fathers.

chat.says: If someone converts to Judaism, can they really pray 'God of our fathers'?
options: Yes. Maimonides wrote that Abraham is their father too, so they say it as written.
Only after many years in the community; until then they stay silent there.
They can, but converts aren't named anywhere in the daily prayers.
